mode_evidence: Shadow method ends in looking at the sky and seeing a grey figure; the third-eye verse says 'he then perceives a fire brilliant like lightning' and the great yogi 'beholds light, pure as holy mountain'. The third-eye verse begins with 'constantly thinks', so that one crosses from imagination to perception.
onset_evidence: Shadow invocation is an explicit trial for a beginner: at sunrise or by moonlight gaze at the neck of your shadow, then look into the sky; if a full grey figure appears it is auspicious. Third-eye verse: keep thinking one has a third eye in the middle of the forehead until a lightning-like fire is perceived. Daily practice; 'by practising it always, he begins at last to see it in his heart'. Teaching is a great secret, given only to qualified yogis. Three years mentioned for success of qualified practitioners.

conditions.posture: Padmasana for the nose-tip gaze and third-eye exercise.
conditions.gaze_or_eye_position: Steady gaze on neck of shadow, then up to sky; gaze on tip of the nose; attention between eyebrows.
conditions.setting: Rising sun or moonlight, clear sky.
conditions.duration_and_schedule: Daily; light contemplated day and night for the Siddha result; success in three years for qualified practitioners.
conditions.prerequisites: Qualified yogi; devotion to God and Guru, free of serious illness.

stages.label: shadow in the sky
stages.description: A full grey shadow seen in the sky is auspicious; with constant practice it is eventually seen in the heart.

what_to_do_with_light: Contemplate it continually; by it sins are destroyed and Siddhas are seen; lie down and contemplate it to remove weariness.
cautions: Yoga to be kept secret and revealed only to those with all the qualifications of a yogi.
interpretation: The seen shadow is a divine reflection (Pratika) giving God's sight; the light is a spiritual light that destroys sins and gives lordship over the light.
practice_summary: Siva Samhita chapter 5 gives two seen-light methods. Pratikopasana: at sunrise or by moonlight, with a clear sky, fix the gaze steadily on the neck of your own shadow, then look up into the sky; seeing a full grey shadow there is auspicious, and daily practice gives long life and finally sight of it in the heart. Third-eye exercise: seated in Padmasana, constantly think that you have a third eye, the eye of Shiva, in the middle of the forehead; you then perceive a fire brilliant like lightning; contemplate this light day and night and you will see the Siddhas. Gaze at the tip of the nose in Padmasana and the yogi beholds a pure light, becoming its lord and guardian. Lie down and contemplate the light to remove fatigue.

key_passages.anchor: At the time of the rising sun, or by moon, let him steadily fix
key_passages.paraphrase: Gaze steadily at the neck of the shadow thrown, then look into the sky; a full grey shadow is auspicious.
key_passages.quote: At the time of the rising sun, or by moon, let him steadily fix his-gaze on the neck of the shadow he throws ; then, after sometime, let him look, into the sky ; ;ifhe sees a full grey shadow in the sky, itis auspicious.

key_passages.anchor: By practising it always, he begins at last to see it in his heart
key_passages.paraphrase: Persistent practice moves the figure from the sky to the heart.
key_passages.quote: 21.. By practising it always, he begins at last to see it in his heart, and the persevering Yogi gets liberation.

key_passages.anchor: he then perceives a fire brilliant like lightning
key_passages.paraphrase: Constantly thinking one has a third eye in the forehead, one perceives a lightning-bright fire; thinking of it day and night brings sight of Siddhas.
key_passages.quote: When the Yogi constantly thinks that he has got a third eye-the eye of Shiva-in the middle of his forehead, he then perceives a fire brilliant like lightning.

key_passages.anchor: The great Yogi beholds light, pure as holy mountain
key_passages.paraphrase: Gazing on the nose tip in Padmasana, the yogi beholds pure light and becomes its lord.
key_passages.quote: 50. The great Yogi beholds light, pure as holy mountain (Kail&s), and through the force of his exercise in it, he becomes the lord and guardian of the light.

key_passages.paraphrase: The teaching is secret and for qualified yogis only.
key_passages.quote: 42. This Yoga is a great secret, and not to be given to every body ; it might be revealed to him only, in whom all the qualifications of a yogi are perceived.
